summary: Iteration 9 tests PASS — 16/17 backend + full frontend smoke. New endpoints work: POST /api/accounts/link/{link_id}/sync returns 401 without bearer, 400 for invalid ObjectId, 404 for other user's link_id / nonexistent id, 400 with detail "Sync not supported for provider 'file'" for file-provider links, and 200 with {synced:int, errors:list} for SimpleFIN links (decrypt-fail path returns 200 with errors[] populated — verified idempotent second call still 200 with synced=0). POST /api/accounts/snaptrade/callback returns 401 without bearer and 503 'SnapTrade not configured' when inert. app.json scheme='jaleter' confirmed. Frontend: alex+test1@jaleter.app / password123 login works, /transactions header shows BOTH tx-import (cloud-upload) and tx-add (plus) circular buttons (both 38x38), settings-accounts sheet title is now 'Linked accounts', all 3 link-mode-{simplefin,file,request} buttons render, no red screen on web despite Linking.addEventListener usage. Regression: /api/providers, /api/accounts/link (snaptrade→503, unknown→400), /api/accounts/import (CSV), /api/accounts/all, /api/support/requests, /api/auth/me — all green. Password left at 'password123' (verified via final login=200). ONE PRE-EXISTING BUG SURFACED (marked xfail): simplefin_service.py:96 sf_fetch_accounts does not catch httpx.ConnectError / other httpx.HTTPError — a linked SimpleFIN account whose host is unreachable causes the sync endpoint to return HTTP 500 instead of 200 with errors[]. This is a real user-facing risk (transient network / bank outage) and was inherited from previous iterations; the new per-link route inherits it verbatim. See action_items.

minor.issue: sf_fetch_accounts (simplefin_service.py:96) does NOT wrap httpx transport errors (ConnectError, ReadTimeout, RemoteProtocolError, etc.) as SimpleFinError. When a SimpleFIN host is unreachable or times out, _sync_docs (server.py:488-518) only catches SimpleFinError, so the httpx exception bubbles up and FastAPI returns HTTP 500. Repro: seed a linked_accounts doc with a validly-Fernet-encrypted access_url pointing to a non-existent DNS host → POST /api/accounts/link/{id}/sync → 500 Internal Server Error + Traceback in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log ending in `httpx.ConnectError: [Errno -2] Name or service not known`. Expected per review spec: 200 with {synced:0, errors:[{link_id, error}]}. Fix: in simplefin_service.fetch_accounts, wrap `r = await client.get(...)` in `try/except httpx.HTTPError as e: raise SimpleFinError(f'SimpleFIN unreachable: {e}') from e`. Same fix should also cover claim_setup_token().

ui_bugs.issue: Touch target is 38x38 — below Apple HIG minimum 44x44. Both header buttons on /transactions and every link-sync/link-remove row button in the Linked-accounts sheet inherit this size (s.circleBtn). Not blocking, but fingers will occasionally miss on small devices.

issues: Console warnings on every screen mount: `"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"` and `props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents`. Non-blocking but will become errors on future RN versions.

action_items: P1: Harden simplefin_service.fetch_accounts (and claim_setup_token) to catch httpx.HTTPError and raise SimpleFinError instead — otherwise any transient bank/SimpleFIN outage returns HTTP 500 to the mobile client and the frontend's green 'Refreshed' toast will never fire; the per-link sync endpoint currently promises 200+errors[] but does not honor that when the underlying transport fails.
P3: Bump CircleBtn size from 38x38 to 44x44 (Apple HIG / WCAG 2.5.5) so tx-import, tx-add, link-sync-*, link-remove-* meet minimum touch targets on small phones.
P3: Migrate remaining `shadow*` StyleSheet props to `boxShadow` and `pointerEvents` prop to `style.pointerEvents` to silence RN-Web deprecation warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:473-485 (new /api/accounts/link/{link_id}/sync route): correctly validates ObjectId (400), scopes lookup by user_id (404), rejects non-simplefin providers (400 with provider name in detail). Clean.
server.py:488-518 (_sync_docs helper): only catches SimpleFinError inside the per-doc loop; bare httpx exceptions escape → 500. See P1 action item.

server.py:544-557 (/api/accounts/snaptrade/callback): correct inert 503 path, but the route is defined BEFORE `_provider_registry = build_registry(db)` on line 561, which works only because the handler is called after startup. Consider moving `_provider_registry` initialization above the callback route for clarity, or lazy-init inside the handler.

app/index.tsx:1232-1244 (Linking effect): correctly guards with `Linking.getInitialURL().then(...)` and returns the subscription remove(). On web the event never fires, which is fine — verified no crash on page load.

app/index.tsx:1105-1110 (AccountLinkSheet YOUR ACCOUNTS rows): link-sync-{link_id} button is only rendered for simplefin rows; file/import rows only get link-remove — matches backend contract (file provider 400s on sync).
app/index.tsx:667-670: tx-import CircleBtn shows the hourglass-outline icon while importing — good UX feedback. Uses expo-document-picker; multipart POST to /api/accounts/import.

rca_of_issue: PRE-EXISTING BUG (surfaced by this iteration's new per-link sync route, though it also affects the batch /api/accounts/sync endpoint): simplefin_service.py:62 and :96 use `async with httpx.AsyncClient(...)` and call `.get(...)` without try/except. Only the HTTP status branches (401/429/other) are converted to SimpleFinError. Any transport-layer failure (DNS resolution, TCP refused, TLS handshake, read timeout) raises httpx.HTTPError → propagates through _sync_docs (which only catches SimpleFinError) → FastAPI serializes as 500. Mitigation (main agent should implement): wrap the `.get(...)` calls in `try/except httpx.HTTPError as e: raise SimpleFinError(f'SimpleFIN unreachable: {e}') from e`. Reproduction: seed linked_accounts with `access_url_encrypted = Fernet(SIMPLEFIN_ENC_KEY).encrypt(b'https://user:pw@nonexistent.invalid.example.test/simplefin').decode()`, then POST /api/accounts/link/{that_id}/sync → 500 with the traceback shown in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log at time of test run.
